resources.string: A hand-picked list for two — with a budget filter and a random pick
Pick a budget and let chance decide — or browse the list yourself.
Tap “Show an idea” and get one date to choose from.
A blanket, popcorn and that film you keep postponing. Phones go to another room.
An hour on familiar streets with no route and no goal — just the two of you.
A blanket, a thermos and something tasty in the park — even a cold day works with a good view.
One round of your favourite game, where the loser makes the tea.
Pick a dish from a cuisine you don’t know and make it together — no rush, with music.
A warm bath, face masks, candles and no chores until morning.
A neighbouring town by train: coffee, a museum and a ticket back in the evening.
Find a band neither of you has heard live and go with no expectations.
One exhibition, one hall and a deal: talk about what you felt, not what you liked.
An hour on the ice, a hot drink afterwards and a photo in front of the lights.
One of you gets up first and brings coffee, pancakes and a handwritten note.
Half an hour outside with a phone and one rule: take funny pictures of each other.
An hour of puzzles — a good test of how well you work as a team.
Ceramics, candles or pasta — leave with something you made with your own hands.
A two-hour rental, the embankment or a park, and a stop wherever you like it.
A show under the dome, then the real stars if the weather agrees.
Slow halls with fish and jellyfish — a good reason not to hurry anywhere.
A duet of the song from your teens, sung loudly and completely off key.
Two lanes, a bit of rivalry and a bet: the loser buys the pizza.
Choose a book for each other blindly — by the cover and the first paragraph.
One city hotel, a late breakfast and zero household chores.
A blanket on the balcony, a sky map app and half an hour without screens.
Evening slots are usually quieter: pick three halls and don’t try to see everything.
An order, chopsticks, a series — and no talk about work.
Clay, a wheel and two crooked cups that will stay on your shelf.
Morning coffee somewhere new before the day starts — a tiny date on a weekday.
A small-stage play and a café talk afterwards — book the tickets in advance.
Steam, a cold shower and herbal tea — two hours just for the two of you.
Get up an hour before dawn, take a thermos and find a spot facing east.
Two tickets to nowhere for the weekend: a new city, a hotel and no plan at all.
